title: Notification Levels on iOS
lede: Profile → Notifications is where people tune what reaches their phone. It used to offer one on/off switch per type; it now offers Off, Silent, or Standard per type, recurring quiet hours, and more ways to pause.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: Same fixture scenario (notifications, Staff user, pause active), same iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator, dark appearance, default text size. The after fixture also carries the new server fields (role catalog, levels, quiet hours) the screen now reads. The simulator clock is live, so the pause end time differs by the 15 minutes between runs.

pairs.title: Top of screen
pairs.sub: Status, pause, and the new quiet hours.
pairs.beforeCap: Pause, then straight into Delivery. No way to silence alerts on a schedule.
pairs.afterCap: Quiet hours sit under Pause: a window, the days it starts on, and whether urgent alerts break through.

pairs.title: After one scroll
pairs.beforeCap: Seven identical switches under one heading. Everything is either on with sound or off.
pairs.afterCap: Quiet hours in full, then Delivery, then types grouped by Gear, Schedule, Account, and Admin.

changes.h: On/off became Off, Silent, or Standard
changes.was: A switch per type. Muting schedule chatter meant losing it entirely.
changes.now: A menu per type. Silent keeps the alert in Notification Center without sound or lighting the screen; Off also stops that type's email.

changes.was: Only a one-off pause, which silenced everything, including overdue gear.
changes.now: A weekly window in Central Time. Alerts still arrive, silently; overdue-gear alerts can break through.

changes.was: The same seven types for everyone, hard-coded in the app.
changes.now: The server sends the types this role actually receives, so staff see item reports and admins see review requests, and new types need no app release.
Adds until tomorrow morning (7 AM) and a custom end time up to 30 days out.

changes.was: Every toggle re-sent the whole preference record.
changes.now: Each change sends only that field; time-wheel edits are batched into one save. Against an older server the screen falls back to the previous switches.

Not in this slice: opening this screen from the iOS Settings link, a settings shortcut in the inbox, and the /settings/notifications deep link.
